# Introduction

The objective of this project is to identify the most successful team in Italian Serie A since 1993.

The data are obtained from the Italy section of the Football-Data website. Each season is stored as a separate CSV file. The analysis focuses on:

- Scraping all Serie A datasets (I1.csv)
- Combining seasons into a single dataframe
- Cleaning the data
- Computing team statistics
- Ranking teams according to points accumulated since 1993

# Challenge 1: Scraping Strategy (No Code)

The website provides one CSV file per season.

The scraping strategy is:

1. Open the Italy page.
2. Extract all hyperlinks.
3. Keep only links associated with Serie A (`I1.csv`).
4. Import every season.
5. Merge all seasons into a single data frame.
6. Keep only the variables required for the analysis.
7. Remove observations with missing dates.

# Challenge 2: Importing and Cleaning the Data

```{r load_data}
library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)

# Scrape all Serie A URLs

page <- read_html("https://www.football-data.co.uk/italym.php")

serie_a_urls <- page |>
  html_elements("a") |>
  html_attr("href") |>
  na.omit()

serie_a_urls <- serie_a_urls[
  str_detect(serie_a_urls, "I1\\.csv$")
]

serie_a_urls <- paste0(
  "https://www.football-data.co.uk/",
  serie_a_urls
) |>
  unique()

# Function to import one season

read_season <- function(url) {

  tryCatch({

    read_csv(
      url,
      show_col_types = FALSE
    ) |>
      select(
        any_of(
          c(
            "Date",
            "HomeTeam",
            "AwayTeam",
            "FTHG",
            "FTAG",
            "FTR"
          )
        )
      )

  }, error = function(e) {

    NULL

  })
}

# Import all seasons

serie_a_master <- serie_a_urls |>
  map(read_season) |>
  compact() |>
  bind_rows()

# Keep valid dates only

valid_matches <- serie_a_master |>
  filter(!is.na(Date))

# Required dataset

valid_dates <- valid_matches |>
  select(
    Date,
    HomeTeam,
    AwayTeam,
    FTHG,
    FTAG
  )

# Summary

cat("Rows before filtering:", nrow(serie_a_master), "\n")
cat("Rows after filtering:", nrow(valid_matches), "\n")
```

## Dataset Preview

```{r}
head(valid_dates)
```

The combined Serie A dataset contains 13,030 observations. After removing observations with missing dates, 11,786 valid matches remain.

# Challenge 3: Historical Team Statistics

To compute team statistics, each match is transformed into two observations:

- One from the home team's perspective.
- One from the away team's perspective.

The match outcome is then classified as a win, loss, or draw.

```{r process_leaderboard}

# Home perspective

home_data <- valid_matches |>
  mutate(
    Team = HomeTeam,
    Outcome = case_when(
      FTR == "H" ~ "Wins",
      FTR == "A" ~ "Losses",
      FTR == "D" ~ "Draws"
    )
  ) |>
  select(Team, Outcome)

# Away perspective

away_data <- valid_matches |>
  mutate(
    Team = AwayTeam,
    Outcome = case_when(
      FTR == "A" ~ "Wins",
      FTR == "H" ~ "Losses",
      FTR == "D" ~ "Draws"
    )
  ) |>
  select(Team, Outcome)

# Team statistics

 team_statistics <- bind_rows(home_data, away_data) |>
  count(Team, Outcome, name = "Count") |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Outcome,
    values_from = Count,
    values_fill = 0
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Matches = Wins + Losses + Draws,
    Points = 3 * Wins + Draws,
    PointsPerMatch = round(Points / Matches, 3)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(Points))
```

## Top 20 Teams

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  head(team_statistics, 20),
  caption = "Top 20 Serie A Teams Since 1993"
)
```

# Results

```{r}
team_statistics |>
  slice(1:10)
```

The ranking is based on the standard football scoring system:

- Win = 3 points
- Draw = 1 point
- Loss = 0 points

# Challenge 4: Come up with at least 3 data questions on the data at hand

What are the most common match scores in Serie A since 1993?

Has the average number of goals scored per match increased or decreased over time?

Which teams perform significantly better at home than away?

Which clubs have spent the most seasons in Serie A since 1993?

# Conclusion

Using all available Serie A matches since 1993, Juventus emerges as the most successful club in the dataset.

Juventus accumulated the highest number of total points and achieved the best overall performance across the period analyzed.

Therefore, based on the available data, **Juventus can be considered the strongest Italian Serie A team from 1993 to the present**.
